chunks: I have come to know of your anger at the posting of al-Ashtar in your place, but I did not do so because of any shortcoming on your part or to get you to increase your efforts, but when I had taken away what was under your authority I would have placed you at a position which would have been less exacting and more attractive to you.

key_terms.الْأَشْتَرِ: Malik al-Ashtar, a prominent companion of Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali replace Malik al-Ashtar with Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr as governor of Egypt?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that his initial reluctance to appoint Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr stemmed not from dissatisfaction with his capability, but from a desire to preserve Malik al-Ashtar’s preeminent status in Egypt. This letter highlights the Imam’s nuanced administrative strategy, balancing meritocracy with political stability, while affirming Ibn Abi Bakr’s trusted position as a capable leader. The passage reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam’s justice in recognizing individual strengths without diminishing others' dignity.
